lesson.title: Sol Forgets the Magic Words: Por Favor & Gracias
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Uh oh — Sol wants a hug, but forgot to say the magic word! Can you help Sol remember?
When you want something, say [[por favor]] — that means 'please'! Ask Sol: '¿Un abrazo, por favor?' (A hug, please?)
When you get something, say [[gracias]] — that means 'thank you'! When Sol gives you a hug, say '¡Gracias!'
You coached Sol to use por favor and gracias — the magic words! Tomorrow, you'll play a sí and no game with Sol.

objectives: Use por favor (please) when requesting something
Use gracias (thank you) when receiving something
materialsNeeded: Sol the puppet (or stuffed animal/toy from Day 1)
A small object to 'give and receive' (toy, snack, or just a hug)
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Have Sol try to take something (a toy, a hug, a snack) without asking politely — pause and look confused, like Sol forgot something.
2. Ask your child: 'What did Sol forget?' Coach them to prompt Sol with por favor.
3. Have Sol ask properly: '¿Un abrazo, por favor?' and give your child a hug or the object.
4. Coach your child to respond with '¡Gracias!' when they receive it.
5. Swap roles — let your child be 'Sol' and forget the magic words, while you coach them.
6. Repeat 3-4 times with different small requests (a toy, a snack, a high-five) until por favor and gracias feel automatic.
7. Close by asking: 'What do we say when we want something? What do we say when we get it?'
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on gracias alone first, since it comes up more often day-to-day; add por favor once gracias feels natural
Ready for more: have your child coach a family member or sibling who 'forgets' the magic words at snack time or during a game
Real-life repetition matters more than a perfect lesson — keep prompting por favor and gracias naturally all week during actual mealtimes and requests
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a role-play coaching activity — success looks like your child prompting 'por favor' before receiving something and saying 'gracias' after, not a written answer.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Extends the week's WA-WL-2015.1.1 Interpersonal Communication target into courtesy formulas, which ACTFL treats as core to interpersonal exchange — introduced here through role-play and coaching rather than direct instruction, since coaching a puppet gives the child ownership of the 'magic words' instead of being lectured about them.

generationData.instructions: Read each line aloud to your child and act it out together.
